A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original ViT plasticity measurements and finetuning experiments on 11 image-classification benchmarks, including accuracies, seed variability, and training dynamics in Section 5 and Appendix D.

after.justification: V3 retains these results and adds DINOv3/GPT2 plasticity measurements, Adam experiments, ViT-Large finetuning, and experiments with restricted training data.

M1.justification: The plasticity measure and component-wise finetuning procedure remain unchanged: each selected component is adapted while other components are frozen. Additional architectures and optimizers extend the evaluation rather than introduce a new proposed method.

E1.justification: V3 extends the image-based plasticity study to language data, using AGNews as a pretraining-distribution proxy and WikiText-103 as downstream data for GPT2 (Appendix E.1.3). The original 11 image benchmarks remain. Restricting existing datasets to 1,000 training samples changes the protocol rather than dataset coverage.

E2.justification: Section 5.2 adds an explicit literature-based comparison with LoRA, quoting Bafghi et al.'s 88.1% Cifar100 result alongside the paper's 89.4% LN2/Adam result. No new LoRA run or matched evaluation protocol is documented. The original component, full-finetuning, and linear-probing comparators remain.

E3.justification: V3 adds Adam/AdamW experiments with learning rates scaled by 0.01 relative to SGD, ViT-Large finetuning, and a protocol using 1,000 training samples and 2,500 steps (Tables 2–3 and 9–10). These are substantial additional evaluation settings; the original SGD learning-rate grid, splits, and checkpoint-selection procedure remain.

E4.justification: V3 adds targeted checks of whether the findings survive changes in optimizer, finetuning model size, and training-data quantity. Adam gradient-norm and validation-loss analyses in Figures 54–58 supplement the retained SGD analyses. DINOv3/GPT2 analyses additionally test the ranking across pretraining paradigms and transformer architectures.

E5.justification: V3 adds tabulated means and standard deviations across learning rates in Tables 9–10, supplementing v1's seed-based uncertainty and graphical hyperparameter distributions. Three-seed reporting, pooled standard errors, and the Wilcoxon test at 5% are retained; the larger total experiment count does not establish more repetitions per setting.

E6.justification: The original component and full-finetuning scores are retained, but all linear-probing scores change between v1 Table 6 and v3 Table 8, including Cifar100 from 65.43 to 67.56 and Clipart from 42.76 to 45.86; Figure 2's relative gains consequently decrease. V3 also adds substantial results for DINOv3/GPT2, Adam, restricted training data, and ViT-Large. These additions concern new conditions, not improvements to the original component scores.

T1.justification: Definition 1, Propositions 1–4, and the mathematical proofs in Appendix B are unchanged. The decoder-only extension discussed in v3 Section 4 was already explained in v1's limitations, including the applicability of Proposition 3 to masked attention.

C1.justification: The introduction broadens the claimed plasticity ranking beyond supervised ViTs to DINOv3 and GPT2, and expands the finetuning contribution to multiple ViT sizes and both SGD and Adam. The central recommendation to prioritize attention and feedforward components remains, but its explicitly claimed empirical scope is substantially wider.

C2.justification: V3 adds a qualification that distillation and instruction alignment may alter plasticity values because they change model weights (Remark 5.2). It also interprets the LoRA comparison as evidence that parameter count alone does not determine performance and removes the earlier vision-only limitation. The main gradient-based mechanism explanation remains unchanged.

D1.justification: V3 newly specifies a 2,000-step warmup, Adam parameters and learning-rate scaling, additional model specifications, and approximately 3,700 GPU hours. It replaces the anonymized my_lib example with the vitef construction API. The repository link already appears in v1, so its repetition is not evidence of newly available code.

R1.justification: V3 adds references supporting the new experiments and comparisons, including DINOv3, GPT2, AGNews, WikiText-103, VTAB, and Bafghi et al., and positions single-component finetuning as competitive with LoRA. The principal related-work discussions and smoothness-based positioning remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: V3 makes localized edits to the abstract, contributions, discussion, affiliations, and publication header. It adds a reproducibility appendix, introduces more experimental subheadings, and reorders the implementation subsections. The main narrative sequence and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: V3 substantially expands the displays with DINOv3/GPT2 plots, Adam training-dynamics figures, and tables for optimizer, model-size, and restricted-data comparisons. Table 1 changes from performance decreases to absolute accuracies with revised highlighting, while Figure 2 receives updated bars and axes. Most earlier appendix plots are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: V1's finetuning evidence was confined to ViT-Base with SGD. V3 directly tests Adam, a larger ViT, and restricted training data, while extending plasticity measurements to self-supervised vision and GPT2. These targeted checks substantially strengthen the generality of the central findings. The benefits outweigh localized reporting defects, notably Table 8 retaining a linear-probing average of 64.22 although its revised rows average approximately 65.82.
